This news article discusses how the car company Ford has changed its opinion about the UK’s zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate. This rule requires carmakers to sell a certain figure of electric cars each year. Back in 2022, Ford was part of a group that strongly supported these rules and even wanted the British government to make the operation stricter so more electric cars would be sold. They believed this would yield good fruit, like better charging infrastructure, and said lowering targets would sing the wrong message to everyone involved. 

Female workers at Ford, along with their colleagues, now face uncertainty as Ford cuts 800 jobs and criticizes the policy it once supported. The dramatic shift in Ford’s perspective shows how the situation for electric cars has changed; there is not as much demand from customers as there was during the pandemic, when interest rates were low and it was much easier for carmakers to sell all the vehicles they produced. Ford did mention earlier that the policy should be reviewed if industry conditions changed, but the reversal is still surprising.

This story is an example of how quickly a company’s public view can change depending on business needs and economic trends, even if it once seemed committed to a certain idea.
